query: What is the evidence that colour-coding tools, containers and cleaning equipment by zone or by material prevents cross-contamination? Cover food processing (allergen control and HACCP zoning with colour-coded utensils and cleaning tools), healthcare (for example the UK NHS national colour coding scheme for cleaning materials), pharmaceutical GMP (dedicated, status-labelled equipment such as 'clean / to be cleaned' tags) and research laboratories. Report measured effects (audits, ATP, microbial or chemical residue results, incident rates), compliance, and failure modes (fading or drifting colours, too many colours, colour-blind staff, colours that mean different things in different schemes), and any recommended number of colours. Cite specific studies and standards.
